$comment: Task plan for AI coding agents. Read AGENTS.md section 7 for how to use this file. Owner: Anderson Mwangi.

project.name: Akili Moto
project.summary: Daily shared trivia challenge with two rounds of ten questions, seven in English and three in Swahili per round, server-scored points, separate round leaderboards, and a combined leaderboard.

rules.pickNext: First task with status todo whose dependsOn tasks are all done.
neverDo: weaken auth or tests to pass a task
invent or generate Swahili words for the answer list or dictionary
send the daily answer to the client before the game is finished

decisions.question: Player identity
decisions.default: Anonymous UUID in a signed HttpOnly cookie, editable unique display name, high-entropy recovery code hashed at rest, no email or password in v1

decisions.question: Durable Objects needed?
decisions.default: No. Attempt limits and concurrency are enforced by database unique constraints

decisions.question: Package layout
decisions.default: Single package with src/worker, src/client, src/shared

decisions.question: Letter model for Swahili
decisions.default: Word length 5, letters a to z only, digraphs (ch, sh, ny, ng and so on) treated as separate letters, ng' stored as ng

decisions.question: Word list source and licensing
decisions.default: Owner supplies answers list and a larger dictionary. Source and licence recorded in docs/WORDLISTS.md. Agent never invents words
alternatives: Licensed open dictionary filtered by the owner

decisions.question: Day boundary
decisions.default: Midnight Africa/Nairobi (UTC+3, no DST), decided by the server

decisions.question: Sheng mode
decisions.default: Out of scope for v1, separate list and mode later

decisions.question: Daily quiz format
decisions.default: Two rounds of ten four-option questions per Nairobi day, seven English and three Swahili per round; both sets are shared and disjoint

decisions.question: Scoring
decisions.default: 100 points for a correct answer and a server-measured speed bonus up to 20 points during the first 20 seconds

decisions.question: Leaderboard ties
decisions.default: Equal point totals share rank; only completed challenges are ranked

decisions.question: Question content review
decisions.default: Sourced starter bank is a draft; owner and fluent Swahili reviewer approve before production

phases.name: Shareable Vercel hosting
phases.goal: Host the browser client on Vercel while keeping the API and D1 on Cloudflare Workers.

tasks.title: Configure Vercel frontend hosting and same-origin API proxy
tasks.description: Publish only the built client on Vercel, proxy /api to the configured production Worker, support exact comma-separated origins in Worker CORS and mutation protection, disable API caching, and document project setup.
acceptance: Vercel publishes only dist/client, so the Worker bundle and server-only question bank are not exposed.
The browser uses a same-origin /api proxy to the configured Cloudflare Worker.
Worker CORS and mutation origin checks accept exact origins from a comma-separated ALLOWED_ORIGIN setting.
API responses are explicitly non-cacheable.
Setup steps explain how to add the Vercel production origin in Cloudflare without wildcard origins.
tasks.notes: Configured locally. Vercel project creation and Cloudflare production variable changes remain owner steps; no deployment or remote mutation was performed. Automated checks were not run in this task.

phases.name: Two-round daily challenge and topic balance
phases.goal: Let each player complete up to two distinct shared rounds per Nairobi day, with fair round and combined rankings and a broad, challenging question mix.

tasks.title: Add two daily rounds, round rankings, and broad question coverage
tasks.description: Hide player management during play. Add a second shared round that unlocks after round one is complete, enforce a maximum of two rounds per player per Nairobi day, use disjoint question IDs across the two rounds, show separate round leaderboards and a combined leaderboard for players who completed both, preserve existing round-one history, and diversify sourced question topics with plausible distractors.
acceptance: A player can complete round one and then round two, but cannot start round two early or create a third round.
Both round sets are deterministic for a Nairobi day, shared across players, and have no question IDs in common.
Round one and round two have separate completed-player leaderboards; the combined leaderboard includes only players who completed both rounds and ranks their summed scores.
Existing completed round-one data is preserved through an additive, locally applied migration.
Player name and recovery controls are absent while playing, while setup and recovery remain available before a round starts.
The current question bank has broad topic tags and balanced topics, retains the seven-English/three-Swahili ratio and increasing difficulty, and uses plausible answer choices.
Question bank content includes institutional sources and remains marked for human review before production use.
tasks.notes: Implemented two shared rounds per Nairobi day, separate round leaderboards, and a combined ranking for players who complete both. Local migration and automated checks passed. Question content is still draft material requiring owner and fluent Swahili review. No production migration or deployment was run.

phases.name: Daily quiz MVP
phases.goal: Deliver a fair, fast daily trivia challenge with server-owned scoring and a shared leaderboard.

tasks.title: Replace Wordle MVP with the daily trivia challenge
tasks.description: Implement the approved ten-question shared daily challenge with a 7 English / 3 Swahili mix, server-side scoring, anonymous answer persistence, and a completed-player leaderboard. Keep the sourced starter bank draft-only pending owner and fluent reviewer approval. Preserve existing Wordle migrations as inactive legacy schema.
acceptance: All players receive the same ten question IDs in the same order for a Nairobi day, with seven English and three Swahili questions.
The client cannot submit score, answer keys, or future question IDs; the server validates sequence and calculates points.
One player cannot score twice for a question through retries or concurrent requests.
The answer, explanation, and source appear only after that question is answered.
Only completed sessions appear in the daily leaderboard; equal scores share rank and responses omit player IDs.
The React app handles loading, error, answer feedback, progress, completion, and leaderboard states on mobile layouts.
The sourced question bank is documented as a draft requiring human review before production.
tasks.notes: Implemented the daily trivia MVP on task/quiz-daily-challenge. Local D1 migration applied. Verification: typecheck passed; lint passed with five non-blocking style warnings; all 27 tests passed; production build and client leak check passed; Cloudflare deploy dry run passed. Question bank remains a sourced draft pending owner and fluent Swahili review. No remote migration or deployment was run.

phases.name: Progressive trivia and polished interface
phases.goal: Make each daily quiz more thoughtful and progressively harder, with an elegant interface and light/dark themes.

tasks.title: Add progressive medium-to-hard trivia and premium light/dark interface
tasks.description: Expand the sourced question pool to 40 draft questions (28 English, 12 Swahili), tag four medium-to-hard levels, and select a stable daily sequence with difficulty increasing across ten positions while preserving the 7:3 language ratio. Keep existing scoring. Redesign the interface in an editorial visual style, add a persistent light/dark theme that follows system preference by default, update contracts and accessible states, and preserve local-only review docs as untracked files.
acceptance: Daily order increases through four explicit levels: medium, challenging, hard, very hard.
Every daily set has exactly 7 English and 3 Swahili questions, the same order for all players, and deterministic selection.
The bank has 40 sourced questions with plausible distractors and reasoning or interpretation; source and explanation are retained.
Existing base points and speed bonus remain unchanged.
Light and dark themes both have accessible contrast, persist a user choice, and default to system preference.
The mobile layout, keyboard operation, reduced motion, live feedback, and language metadata remain accessible.
Question answer keys and future questions remain absent from client assets and API responses.
Local-only docs remain untracked and no D1 migration is required.
tasks.notes: Implemented the 40-item draft bank, deterministic four-level 7:3 daily schedule without repeats, public difficulty metadata, v1 assignment compatibility bank, theme toggle and editorial light/dark design. Existing 100-point score and speed bonus are unchanged; no database migration was needed. Verification passed: typecheck, lint, 32 tests, production build, and client leak scan covering both banks. Owner and fluent Swahili review are still required for the question text, translations, distractors, and sources. Work is on task/Q2-01-progressive-quiz.

phases.name: Player identity and game history
phases.goal: Give players a recoverable unique identity, editable public name, private game history, and a fresh shared question set for each daily game.

tasks.title: Add player profiles, recovery, history, and no-repeat daily sets
tasks.description: Persist unique player profiles with an editable unique display name and hashed recovery code, expose player-scoped history, show names on the leaderboard, and never assign a daily question set more than once. Preserve one shared challenge per Nairobi day and fail closed if the bounded selector cannot find a fresh set.
acceptance: Every active profile has a database-enforced unique UUID and an editable case-insensitively unique display name.
A hashed recovery code restores the same identity and previous records on another browser; raw codes are returned only at creation or rotation.
Players can view their own completed-game history, and requests cannot expose another player's history.
Leaderboard entries show display names without exposing player IDs.

Everyone receives the same daily question set, and a previously assigned set is never reused; the bounded selector fails closed if it cannot find a fresh candidate. D1 enforces uniqueness under concurrent assignment.
The profile, recovery, name, history, and assignment flows have Workers integration tests, including invalid input, cross-player isolation, and concurrency.
Cookie-authenticated writes reject missing or untrusted Origin headers, while the configured browser origin can submit them.
Recovery throttling remains effective for concurrent requests and expired hashed-IP counters are pruned.
The additive D1 migrations apply successfully in production, and the production Worker runs with COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET configured.
tasks.notes: Implemented UUID-backed profiles, unique editable names, recovery-code restoration/rotation, paginated private history, leaderboard names, and database-enforced no-repeat daily set assignment. Recovery uses 160-bit codes stored as SHA-256 hashes; cookie-authenticated writes enforce allowed Origin. Recovery attempts use an atomic D1 counter keyed by hashed client IP. Verification passed: corepack pnpm typecheck, lint, 41 tests, production build and question leak scan. Migrations 0002-0004 were applied locally and in production; the production Worker was deployed with COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET configured. The 0003 backfill was verified. Bounded selector (4,096 candidates) fails closed rather than reusing a set. Needs owner review, including recovery-code handling and production migration against existing remote assignments.

tasks.title: Require player name choice before starting a daily game
tasks.description: Make name selection the initial view. Do not request a quiz session or player history until the player starts; persist a changed name before starting and keep the player on the setup view if saving fails.
acceptance: The initial view asks for a player name and offers an explicit Start action.
New players must replace the generated Player- name before they can start.
Saved player names are prefilled; returning players can start without changing them.
A changed name is persisted before the first quiz request; save failures leave the setup view visible with a clear retry path.
Quiz-session and history queries remain disabled until Start is clicked.
A recovered identity returns to the setup view and must explicitly start before loading its game.
The public UI does not display the internal player UUID; the browser cache stores only the display name and resume preference.
The chosen player name is cached in the same browser and a matching server profile resumes the current daily game.
The name label appears immediately above the input and the setup card uses compact spacing.
tasks.notes: Implemented compact name-first setup, explicit Start, and same-browser resume using a local display name plus resume preference. The server profile must match the cached name before resuming; the player UUID is not stored in the browser cache. Existing named profiles without a cache are treated as returning players; new and recovered profiles remain at setup until Start. Verification passed: corepack pnpm typecheck, corepack pnpm lint, corepack pnpm build including the client leak scan, and git diff --check. Tests were not run.

tasks.title: Assign friendly names and simplify player recovery
tasks.description: Give new players a unique friendly random name on their first visit, allow them to start with it or edit it, keep the saved name when they return in the same browser, and explain recovery in plain language.
acceptance: A new profile receives a friendly English adjective-animal name with a short numeric suffix, generated server-side and protected by the existing case-insensitive unique index.
A player may start with the generated name or replace it with another valid unique name.
Existing profiles retain their current name; returning browsers use the saved server profile name and resume preference.
The setup screen explains that the player name can be changed and appears on the leaderboard.
Recovery copy explains that the code restores the saved name and game history on another device, and that creating a new code replaces the old one.
The recovery form is labeled by the code it requires and the progress it restores, not by the player's display name alone.
tasks.notes: Implemented server-generated friendly names with collision retries, retained existing profile names, allowed starting unchanged, preserved same-browser resume behavior, and simplified recovery copy. Verified with corepack pnpm typecheck (passed), corepack pnpm build (passed, client leak check passed), and git diff --check (passed). corepack pnpm lint reports 22 repository-wide formatting diagnostics; focused Biome found the same baseline CRLF formatting issues and one import order issue, which was corrected. Tests were not run. Human review required. Follow-up review: added unit tests for name format and validation (test/player-names.test.ts), repository tests for case-insensitive collision retry, returning-player name retention and fail-closed exhaustion (test/player-repository.test.ts), and a friendly-name assertion on profile creation; fixed one Biome formatting issue in GamePage.tsx. Verified with corepack pnpm typecheck (passed), corepack pnpm test (47 passed), corepack pnpm build (passed, client leak check passed). The 22 repository lint diagnostics are CRLF line endings from the Windows checkout (core.autocrlf=true); committed files are LF. Second follow-up: a first-time player never auto-resumed (pressing Start rewrote the cached profile, which re-ran the new-player branch and reset resume to false), and the recovery code vanished on any profile refetch. Resume is now decided once per player id through decideResume, and the profile query keeps the code for the same player for the page session (never stored). Unit tests cover both; the once-per-player effect guard has no DOM test.
